Chris help a seabird named Bill on Christmas Island. A Shih Tzu, arrives in respiratory distress. Meanwhile, Tim heads to the zoo to give a feisty resident a pedicure. Chris finds out if cavoodle Lola’s bark is worse than a bite.

Tim wants Chris to find out why Jack the koala has suddenly developed nasty bumps all over his face. They take him to the local clinic for an immediate biopsy. When the results come back Tim is astonished to learn that Jack has acne.

A dairy buffalo called Penny has severely deformed horns, which are growing into her skull, dangerously close to her brain. Chris has to try to corral the timid 10 year old, and then carry out the painstaking job of carefully removing the horns.

Chris heads out to sea to save an endangered grey nurse shark entangled in fishing line with a hook in its gob. He's joining a specialist rescue team in the water to corral the injured shark and bring it to the surface.

Chris is helping at the Marlin Coast veterinary hospital in Cairns. His first patient is a young dog which has had a nasty encounter with a hedge cutter. Misty has ended up with deep cuts across her nose. How the young dog avoided more disastrous injuries is a miracle.

Chris is helping at the Marlin Coast veterinary hospital in Cairns, and his first patient is a rare Fijian iguana Called Ako. The Iguana hasn't been himself and isn't eating properly. Chris needs to do an x-ray to try to work out what's going on. The results reveal a massive bladder stone inside the small animal, and he needs immediate surgery.

A frail joey orphan's brought in after his mum was hit by a car. Sandy's determined to give the little battler a chance, and Chris faces a challenge repairing his broken leg—it's heart-stopping when he finds if the risky surgery worked.

Andrew investigates a worrying lump on a horse for a possible killer disease, but can he get close enough to find out? And Doctor Rachel is feeling the pressure when a passionate wildlife warrior brings in two distressed little Aussies.
Romi faces multiple emergencies when Lucy the groodle crashes before and during surgery, and Andrew treats a seriously ill goat that could be infested with a life-threatening parasite.

Andrew must make a life-and-death decision on a close friend’s pet cow. Rachel investigates why a friendly young Labrador has developed a worrying limp, but can she calm her terrified patient down enough to even treat him?

On this episode, a critically ill kangaroo infant has Andrew and the young joey’s rescuer worried for its life. Dr. Romi has her hands full with eight lively puppies, but will they get a clean bill of health?
On this episode, delicate surgery has Andrew anxious for Sally the cow’s future. And why is Doctor Romi so over the moon?

p.t: The Secret of the Mona Lisa
p.d: The Mona Lisa by Leonardo da Vinci is one of the most famous paintings in the world. Her real name according to art history is La Gioconda. For many years though, there have been doubts: why did Leonardo not hand the portrait on to the commissioner if it was a picture of his wife?
Xialong Zhang and Cao Guangzhi are two Chinese nationals who are caught attempting to steal proprietary information from Apple Inc., and Tesla's Autonomous driving vehicle for a Chinese competitor.
In late Victorian England, women began to organize to gain the right to vote. The fight for women's suffrage lasted well into the early 20th Century.

In the 15th century, an inventor in a workshop in Strasburg came up with a machine that would eventually change the history of the entire world and shake a religion to its core. The choice of the first work to be printed is an astute one: Saint Jerome's Latin version of the Bible.

In the 17th century, a long period of civil war in France and war across Europe, rebellious members of the French Parliament, dubbed The Fronde, defy the monarchy and this defiance does not end well for them...and changes the history of France.
How did one man succeed in relaunching the Olympic spirit and turn the Games into a global event?

Allied Special Forces launched daring wartime missions to capture or kill Nazi generals where they were stationed on the front lines of war. This film captures the real-time drama felt as the Special Forces ordered these dangerous and complicated missions to exotic locations.

p.d: The Mona Lisa by Leonardo da Vinci is one of the most famous paintings in the world. Her real name according to art history is La Gioconda. For many years though, there have been doubts: why did Leonardo not hand the portrait on to the commissioner if it was a picture of his wife?

Finding the point of intersection between the old world and the new along the coast of Gabon. The idea is a romantic one, but what Gabon is now is still central to a lot of Surfer's notions: untouched wilderness, the last stand of certain species, the last outpost of languages and cultures.
S2 E3Liberia Surf adventurers, Shannon and Shayne McIntyre, set off for the remote West African coastline of Liberia to surf and lend a helping hand to efforts inside this post-war country.

p.t: Camp Woodward: Meet the New Kids
p.d: S4 E1Meet the new kids of season four, Chad (BMX), Alex (Skate) and Lucky (Skate). We find out why they are attending the best sports camp, Camp Woodward, in Pennsylvania this summer.

S4 E2The new kids arrive at Camp Woodward in Pennsylvania. Chad, Alex and Lucky meet up with old friends, meet new friends, participate in a skate/BMX demo, and take a quick trip to the emergency room.

p.t: Built to Shred: Surf Rail of Death 2
p.d: S3 E13Jeff King and the crew try to make lightning strike twice and this Surf Rail proves to be a lot harder than the last.

p.t: Built to Shred: Shred Ranch RIP
p.d: S4 E1It's the end of an era as host Jeff King's beloved Shred Ranch in Encinitas is demolished. Join him and the Built to Shred crew, with special guests Tony Hawk, Bob Burnquist, Bucky Lasek, Neal Mims, Mike.

p.t: The Standard Snowboard Show: Burton Hemsedal
p.d: S3 E7At the end of every snowboard season, Burton Snowboards puts on incredible park sessions in Hemsedal, Norway. After the resort closes they open it up again solely for top snowboarders, photographers, filmers and cat drivers to make whatever snow features they desire.  This episode compiles some of the best footage shot over the years at the Burton Hemsedal sessions along with the world record for the biggest park jump by Mads Jonsson. If you like shredding the park at the local resort than you will love the show.

p.t: The Standard Snowboard Show: Lake Tahoe
p.d: S3 E8Go back to the early days of freestyle snowboarding in Lake Tahoe.  From the uprising of riders from the Grass Valley scene and the opening of Squaw Valley to snowboarding and the conflicts that evolve from taking over the mountain.  This episode covers it all from the snowboard legends first hand and the tricks that made them famous.

p.t: The Adventures of Danny and the Dingo: Mountain Creek
p.d: S1 E4Danny's ex-girlfriend, Thania, joins the tour for the 3rd stop, Mountain Creek. The crew heads to the mountain and squeezes some snowboarding of their own in, before judging the first night's rail contest. Day 2 of Mountain Creek proves to be the best competition yet, and Danny's father signs on to be a judge along with another home town hero, Sketchy D. The 3rd trip to Grenade games is won by Timmy Kempson, who takes the crew to his house and shows off his backyard training facilities. Upon returning to Mountain Creek the next day to pick up the RV, they discover that a snowboard instructor has broken into the bus and stolen their gloves. After saying good by to Danny's parents and ex-girlfriend, the gang heads to the final Zumiez signing, in Long Island, where bus driver, Dawain, gets everyone lost for hours.

p.t: The Adventures of Danny and the Dingo: Layover In Cleveland
p.d: S1 E5The boys finish their last Zumiez signing in Long Island. On the way to Raging Buffalo they decide to stop halfway in Cleveland.  Dawain, the bus driver, gets lost and begins driving in circles around Manhattan. Carolla, the camera man, takes charge of the Grenade RV and suggests that they drive straigistake of giving the producer a wedgie in which he retaliates with permanent reht to his mothe's house in Cleveland. The gang is in for a surprise when a very energetic mother greats everyone with Apple-cran martinis at 9am. After spending the morning at Carolla's mother's house, Danny, Dingo and Lucas decide to get tattoos. Lucas makes the msults for Lucas. With one stop left to go, the gang heads to the final stop Raging Buffalo and gets day 1 underway. That night the boys decide to go for a nice meal. At the table Goon takes a joke a little too far triggering Dingo into hitting Lucas so hard a lump the size of a golf ball forms on his forehead.

One day. One swell. No second chances. Capítulo Perfeito 2026 gathers the world's leading tube riders and waits for the ocean to deliver flawless conditions. Once the call is made, every barrel demands instinct, commitment and precision in the ultimate search for surfing perfection.

The path to perfect waves starts with the ones you'd rather avoid. Suffering, setbacks and unwanted rides shape your resilience, making the reward feel earned. By facing what's uncomfortable, surfers eventually reach what they truly desire-the waves that make it all worthwhile.
S2 E6The campers close out their final days of camp and have tons of fun. Cody , Larry , and Hunter all reflect back on their Camp Woodward experience.

A film about the life and philosophy of perhaps the most impactful surf film of all time: Morning of the Earth. 50 years after its 1972 release, filmmaker Albert Falzon reflects on a lifetime of living in the present. With newly uncovered footage from the original, and with stories from Australia, Hawaii, and pristine Bali, this is a celebration of 50 years around the sun.

It's hard to know what's haunting the Cumberland Library and Monastery in Rhode Island. It could be nine settlers who were skinned alive and buried there in the 1600s. Or it could be the inhabitants of a monastery used for generations. Currently a library, people report voices, doors opening and slamming, and shadowy, floating monks around the property. Adam and Amy encounter something that turns the faucets on and off in a bathroom.

TAPS travels to Brunswick, Ga., to investigate the Brunswick Old City Hall, where an officer was killed in the 1890s; next, the team heads to a former worsted mill, where the caretaker is on edge and insists that the location be kept a secret.

The TAPS team explore an abandoned school in Barnegat, N.J., looking into reports that the apparition of a beloved teacher who died in 1965 is luring children inside the building. Later, they arrive in Clay County, Fla., on a mission to discover if an old courthouse and jail is haunted by the ghosts of inmates and a murdered sheriff.

TAPS return to the Trans-Allegheny Lunatic Asylum in Weston, West Virginia, for their 200th episode, which finds the team reunited with Grant, Dustin and Joe. Efforts are made to reach former patients who suffered tragic lives in the hospital.
TAPS visits Cincinnati Music Hall on Halloween to uncover whether the thousands of people buried under the building are playing paranormal tricks.
Some new, and old cast members participate in the investigation of the Wild Turkey Distillery in Kentucky. The TAPS team looks for traces of the ghosts of the founding family members.

The Atlantic Paranormal Society travels to New York to investigate unexplained activity at the Culinary Institute of America, where many believe the spirits of Jesuit priests roam the area where they once lived when the institute was once a seminary.
To set a bride-to-be's mind at ease, TAPS checks out the venue where her wedding will be held. Then, the team examines a Connecticut mansion.
TAPS travels to the historic St. Charles, Missouri to investigate Main Street’s hauntings.

The team investigate the Burlingame and Chaffee Opera House in Carthage, Mo.; and they visit a private residence in Connecticut to help a family who believe a presence has taken over their home and children.

TAPS travel to Missouri to help three generations of a family living on what they believe to be a haunted estate; and in Massachusetts, the team investigate whether one ghost is connected to two different properties.

The Atlantic Paranormal Society travels to Rhode Island to help owners of two allegedly haunted theaters investigate two buildings to learn if the spirits that are possibly occupying the second building is traveling between the two locations.

TAPS investigates Fort Adams in Newport, RI where the caretaker says visitors are jabbed and have rocks thrown at them. He's hoping the team can determine who the spirits are and what ear they come from. The investigators have numerous experiences including hearing footsteps; K.J. is twice touched at two different locations. Their recorders also pick up knocking sounds and a child's ghostly voice.
TAPS examines the Houghton Mansion in Massachusetts, where a tragic 1914 car crash that claimed four lives may have left restless spirits behind.

TAPS investigates at Southern Vermont College in Bennington. According to legend, the wife of the school's founder committed suicide when learning about his affair with the nanny, who, it's said, hanged herself. Witnesses report a white mist in the library, as well as voices and self-opening windows. Orbs and voices are also reported in a nearby dorm. The team collects evidence they believe points to a residual haunting.

You've seen her in the kitchen before, but this time it's Jeni's turn to show off her culinary skills. Jeni, joined by her close friends and family, is cooking up some of her favourite autumn foods.

Join Joy Ravela as she challenges Eloise Packham and Leanna Cooper about their phone addiction! How much do they depend on their phones? How do they model phone use to their family and friends? Their answers may surprise you!
The church of Tonga demands donations, especially from those who have left the country.

All around the world the power of the Gospel is shared by ordinary people facing extraordinary obstacles. Believers in every part of the world face unique challenges. Travel around the globe to Estonia, Colombia and Taiwan with Franklin Graham as they witness the impact and change in lives as the host the Festival of Hope.

Pastor Joseph Prince preaches dynamic messages centred on the pure gospel of the grace of God. His desire is to help believers understand grace and how greatly blessed, highly favoured and deeply loved they are by their heavenly Father.

Direct from Houston, Texas, USA; join Joel and Victoria Osteen and the team from Lakewood Church, for this program of powerful music and empowering preaching. Experience from the weekend church service of Lakewood Church, the largest and fastest growing church in America that is inspiring millions of people around the world!
The annual evangelism conference led by Ray Comfort and the Living Waters crew.
Ever wonder why love can be painful? Today, Joyce reveals how dying to self brings freedom, healing, and growth, leading to a changed life through love.
With Duke's return fast approaching, Dani realises her job is on the line; she questions God's path for her as she discovers her ex-fiance is back in town and faces a family emergency.
As Dani returns to work after her dad's health scare, she and Griffin reinstate the Epic Fail Club; Ashley receives some news that could change her and Andy's future.

Dani navigates Hunter being back in town while Tim heads out on a call that leads him to a new romance; Marcos hosts the grand opening of his art gallery before someone's mistake causes the event to go awry.
Dani ups her game at work knowing she has limited time left; Duke continues his sobriety journey; Ashley makes an important discovery while Dani opens up to Tim about her past with Hunter.

Direct from Houston, Texas, USA; join Joel and Victoria Osteen and the team from Lakewood Church, for this program of powerful music and empowering preaching. Experience from the weekend church service of Lakewood Church, the largest and fastest growing church in America that is inspiring millions of people around the world!

The In Touch program reaches the world with the Gospel with messages that tackle such issues as parenting, finances, personal crises, emotions, and relationships. Dr. Stanley fervently believes the Bible to be the inerrant Word of God, a belief strongly reflected in his teaching. Dr Charles Stanley is the author of more than 50 books.
Join Pastor Steven in the Basin where he digs deep into scripture and breaks down the Word of God in these short conversational teachings.

With only 30 minutes and the clock ticking, can Vanessa make an allergen friendly meal for 4 for about 40 bucks? On the menu: kale and lentil salad with green goddess dressing, chickpea curry, and avocado key lime pie cups!

“A” is on the menu and Chef Robert Jewell takes on this meal challenge with apricots and avocados. First up, Robert cooks a spicy roasted quail and drizzles it with some sweet apricot and calvados sauce. Next, is a meal best served cold! Robert slices up sushi-grade tuna and transforms it into a flavourful tartare, brought to life by rich avocado and refreshing lime. On the side, he adds crusty crostini with savoury soy sauce and sesame oil, the perfect complement for this meltin- your-mouth meal. For his final dish, Robert combines apricots and avocados for an unbelievably tasty dish.

Unlock Gusto TV's top recipes on QR Countdown! Thousands of viewers scan our QR codes to access our delicious dishes. Now. we're serving up 8 of our most popular recipes featuring honey. from hosts like Shahir Massoud and Jessica McGovern.

Chef Kyle Crawford pulls back the curtain on sour sauces! First a brown butter picatta sauce for chicken picatta! Next, a smoked tomato ponzu sauce for fried oysters and a duo of orange marmalade and lemon curd for crepes!

Tacos take a turn on the griddle, blending time-honored tradition with new inspiration. Crisped tortillas, inventive fillings, and vibrant toppings come together in a celebration of the world’s most versatile handheld meal.
Vanessa Gianfrancesco creates an international menu with brunch recipes from around the world.

Vanessa prepares for four busy weeknight dinners by cooking different dishes in her multi-cooker, including Korean beef tacos, split pea soup, a roasted chicken stuffed with rosemary and other fresh herbs, and a chicken pot pie.
Vanessa Gianfrancesco loves to cook and feed people because it feeds her soul. Learn how to host while being conscious of time, money, and how a little inspiration can elevate any meal.

Fast and flavorful come together as griddles work overtime to deliver delicious meals in under thirty minutes. Quick cooking meets bold taste, showing that great food can be effortless, even on the busiest of days.

Chef-host Shahir Massoud tries out recipes from Your Pasta Sucks: A “Cookbook” by comedian Matteo Lane! Follow along as Shahir prepares eggplant parmigiana, pasta alla pesto trapenese, and risotto allo zafferano!
Piemonte cuisine is influenced by its mountainous terrain. Chef Michael Bonacini shows us how to make its warm regional dishes like Bagna Cauda.
Cooking doesn’t always have to bring the heat. Chef and fish lover Spencer Watts shows you how to prepare cold dishes with arctic char and shrimp.
Chef Spencer Watts has fun wrapping some of his favorite seafood to create delicious dishes with swordfish and shrimp.

Desiree Nielsen makes healthy meals with vegetable juice, then she serves a simple avocado toast and a strawberry balsamic toast with ricotta, next she makes veggie burgers filled with spinach and basil, and bakes a classic carrot cake with a twist.

Desiree Nielsen shows some easy-to-make healthy home cooked dishes, such as breakfast with eggs and spiralized fried potatoes, for lunch, a protein rich fonio pilaf with grilled asparagus and finally she cooks up some creamy macaroni and cheese.
Witness two different reactions when a mother and daughter discover ghosts.
Victor and Katrina fight back against the malignant spirits threatening their homes and even their lives.
Meet friends who experience and respond to the supernatural in different ways.
Follow Paul and Diana along the open highway, where they encounter angelic beings that turn their trip into a once-in-a-lifetime journey.
Get to know Deborah and Jay, who come from families that see spirits and have ghostly encounters of their own.
Witness the power of ghosts when once influences Stephen to end his marriage.
See how families react when kids say they’ve seen a ghost.
Hear from two people who’ve been to the other side and lived to tell the tale.
Visit an apartment haunted by ghosts who once committed a crime there.
Paranormal investigator Erin Goodpipe gets to the bottom of Bathsheba rumors.
Paranormal investigator Erin Goodpipe tries to see who haunts Old Arnold Estate.

The Chestnut House in Manchester, Kentucky, has a macabre history as its role as a casket storage facility and tales of spectral voices and apparitions, and its paranormal past may be real or just a ruse to attract attention.

Step into Perryville Battlefield's Karrick-Parks House, where 7,600 Civil War spirits are said to linger. Meet the town's re-enactors as the team launches a bold experiment to document long-dead soldiers.

The team conducts a split investigation and explore the eerie H.P. Bottom House, which resonates with the echoes of Civil War battles and they test a possible correlation between two historical homes that witnessed unspeakable horrors.

Face chilling challenges in the terrifying Benton farmhouse. Go head to head with a shape-shifter on the prowl, catch whispers in the air, witness unseen hands at play, and discover a historic secret just waiting to be unravelled.

The chefs compete in their first team challenge prepping squid. At dinner service, one team overcomes a difficult start to finish strongly, while the other struggles to remember tickets and has disasters with raw chicken.

The teams go head to head in a speed challenge, serving Paris Hotel employees, with a special treat for the winners and a day of pastry for the losers. Dinner service provides problems for both teams, with everything going wrong.
Chef Ramsay mixes up the teams, and there is a communication challenge for the chefs to get their teeth into, with an exciting reward for the winners.
The teams compete to have their dishes chosen for Chef Ramsay's daughter's birthday party - with surfing at Planet Hollywood an extra incentive for the winner.
Chef Ramsay shakes up the teams ahead of an international cuisine challenge. At dinner service, one team starts strongly, while the other makes some catastrophic errors.
The challenge pushes the chefs' ability to work together to the limit, with one team enjoying a luxurious day out as a prize, and the other having to sift through garbage.

The chefs compete in a Spells Kitchen competition where they play for ingredients and then cook with them, with the winners enjoying a hot tub reward. Service is a charity special with guests Brad Garret and Deion Sanders.
The chefs take part in the infamous blind taste test, but there is a shock in store for one of the winning team.
The chefs compete in a dating-app themed challenge, where they must combine hand-selected ingredients and a random one into the perfect match, with the winning team being treated to a spa day.
It's Black Jacket Day for the seven remaining chefs as they compete in three challenges in hopes of winning one of the coveted five black jackets that are up for grabs.
Gordon Ramsay challenges the chefs to create dishes that not only taste good, but look the part as well, with his social-media followers choosing a winner.
The final four Young Guns compete in the first ever Hell's Kitchen Beach BBQ, but whose food will the party-goers enjoy the most? At dinner service, each chef has a chance at running the pass.

The final three chefs are instructed to create their own menus for the final challenge and are paired with the sous chefs to think up stunning meals. However, a night on the town with Chef Ramsay has a surprise in store.

Hell's Kitchen Young Guns Season 20 comes down to Trenton and Megan, battling for the head chef role at Gordon Ramsay Steak 2.0 in Vegas. With their brigades assembled and Ramsay's guidance, they cook their final dinner service.

The new chefs enter Hell's Kitchen and cook their signature dishes for Ramsay. It's men versus women, and the first service is a total disaster. Ramsay shuts the kitchen down and the red team lose a member.
Dave and Jenny turn a movie-loving couple's builder-grade house into a customised home that features a movie theatre in the attic.
Now that their kids are grown, two Arizona teachers are ready to pursue their dream of opening a bed and breakfast in Sarlat-la-Canéda, France.
Tarek's friend, Robert, wants to get into flipping and they buy a home sight unseen in Lakewood, CA.
Real estate and flipping expert Christina Anstead helps clients transform their outdated properties into high-end homes in Southern California.
A team of long-time friends and first-time flippers is tackling an ambitious first project: an almost 3,000-square-foot home in View Park.

p.d: In this final special episode, David revisits the early winners who started it all to see how life has changed since their big wins.

Take in the moving stories of those who experienced the ferocity of German bombing, as the Luftwaffe targeted the major cities of Britain.

By May 1940, the die was cast and the war started in earnest. This episode examines the buildup to the Battle of Britain, studying the technological advances that the RAF pioneered, to the start of the Battle itself. At the heart of the RAF production were two world-class fighters, the Hurricane and the Spitfire, which were able to compete against the best the Luftwaffe had to offer.

This episode focuses on events from July to early September, 1940. The Germans tried initially to bomb British naval shipping with limited success. However, three separate attacks in August targeting RAF airfields were successful. Biggin Hill, North Weald, and Kenley were all temporarily put out of action. Then, the Germans made a mistake that ultimately lost them the war.

During the first week of September, Hitler decided to move the bombing strategy away from the airfields, to civilian London. This episode examines the spirit of the Londoners who defied Hitler, and ultimately ended the war in the last weeks of September. The RAF, with fewer resources, fewer men, and fewer machines, had beaten the might of the Luftwaffe.

Put on your dancing shoes as the Zeimers’ daughters hunt for a puppy who loves to bop as much as they do. Learn whether a West Highland terrier, Havanese, or French bulldog has the moves to win their hearts and secure a place in their family.

Get to know the Smith family, who are in the market for their very first family dog. Visit with three friendly puppies who could be the perfect match for these beginners: an adorable linnois, a cuddly barbet, and a playful cairn-Westie cross.
Chris and Lisa head to fire-ravaged Blue Mountains to help stranded animals. Chris treats a premature baby alpaca whose mum went into early labour during evacuation. The newborn cria is fading fast.

Hit the road with Will, who’s guiding a five-tonne elephant to a new home, and juggle the demands of two orphaned baboons with Debbie. Experience a triumph as marine biologist Alison returns critically endangered African penguins to their ocean home.

Grab your lab coat for Jenna and Sean’s unique experiment: testing if elephants’ and meerkats’ super sniffers can detect the deadly puff adder’s scent. Join Emma’s pangolin rehab session and face a dazzle of zebras with vet Annie and volunteer Will.

Join the hunt for a moose on the loose who’s raising a ruckus in the neighbourhood. Back at the farm, a permanent resident has become a loveable nuisance. Special guests arrive at the rehab center bearing a treat for Hope’s dedicated volunteers.

See Chris help a seabird named Bill on Christmas Island. Patchy Girl, a Shih Tzu, arrives in respiratory distress. Meanwhile, Tim heads to the zoo to give a feisty resident a pedicure. Chris finds out if cavoodle Lola’s bark is worse than a bite.

Tim wants Chris to find out why Jack the koala has suddenly developed nasty bumps all over his face. When they go to local clinic for an immediate biopsy, Tim is astonished to learn that Jack has acne
A three-legged Labrador has an issue; Scott tries to determine why a two-year-old patient is walking like a senior animal; a chubby hedgehog begins a fitness routine.
Follow Chris to Coffs Harbour, where he examines a rescue dolphin that may have cancer and learns about its 42-year friendship with head trainer Greg.

Meet best friends Tammy and Allie, who are living the dream at Wendigo Farms, with a new business, beautiful horses, and a state-of-the-art barn. Learn why running this operation isn’t all peaches and cream once harsh reality rears its ugly head.

Adam and Jamie test two myths about the power of the zombie hoard. First, can they really break through a door thanks to working as a team of pushing power? Second, what's the perfect weapon to use against the zombie hoard: gun or ax? Then Kari, Grant and Tory unleash their inner beast too as they find out if it's really inevitable that zombies will catch you even though they only shuffle at 2 miles an hour!
The guys test whether it's true that duct tape can be used in place of a seatbelt. Then, the guys are going to attempt to build a trebuchet with nothing but the talented tape and some 2 x 4s.
It’s wall-to-wall automotive mayhem, as the team drive through glass, plough through traffic, and fire an RPG at an SUV to take aim at classic Hollywood crash clichés.
In this ballistics bonanza Adam and Jamie ask if supersonic ping pong can go lethally wrong while Kari, Grant and Tory light the frozen fuse on a cannon made of ice!

On this Mythsion Impossible Episode, the MythBusters try to ‘Herd cats’ and ‘catch a greased pig’, but will these implausible idioms turn out to be true, or can the MythBusters make the impossible possible?
In this ballistics bonanza the team pulls out their sums and ammo to test a classic collection of gun clichés!
On this ‘Moonshiners’ inspired episode, the MythBusters investigate an intoxicating concoction of myths about moonshine.
Myths tested: Do males prefer women with blonde hair? Do pheromone sprays work? Are women attracted to wealthy men? Do men give larger tips to women with larger breasts?

Myths tested: Can watering plants with microwaved water kill them? Can you put out a fire on a lake by turning a boat at an angle? Can metronomes started at different times sync together? Can a ball chain levitate over a lip of a cup?

Myths tested: When two cars try to knock each other off the road does it always result in a long and difficult duel? Is the silver screen trick of tipping up on to two wheels and driving sideways as easy as it seems?
On this Episode of MythBusters, the team go to terrifying extremes and vertigo inducing heights to investigate two adrenaline-pumping myths.

Star Wars provides further fodder when Jamie and Adam see whether high ground really is important in a duel, and whether it's possible to dive out of the way of laser blaster bullets (well, a Stormtroopers', anyway).
On this Episode of MythBusters, the team investigate a horde of household disasters, to find out if home could be where the hurt is!
Fire in the Hole! Hunker in the bunker, the Mythbusters are taking on tinsel town’s explosive credentials.
Stand by for some ballistic backyard bedlam and a gruesome glass guillotine in an episode devoted to accidental ammo!
The African Penguin is the only penguin species that breeds in Africa, and it is found nowhere else.
Surviving the Serengeti is a tale of courage and instinct, of hope and desperation-showing that during the long dry season, carnivores have little to hunt but manage to survive and raise their young.
Europe's biggest terrestrial mammal was hunted to extinction, but thanks to ambitious rewilding, the European Bison has been re-introduced.
The Mekong continues it's journey south marking the Eastern border of heart of South East Asia, Thailand.
Get inspired by the unique healing journeys of abused and exploited elephants.
In this episode, we follow life in one of Africa's elephant orphanages. Thanks to the dedication and passion of a team of the keepers, orphan elephants here are learning to adapt to life in the wild.
Camp Phoenix in Zambia's Kafue National Park is elephant heaven. It has thick forest, open grassland and plenty of water. Here a herd of orphan elephants are being given another chance.
Observe the fragile and evolving friendship between humans and elephants.
South Africa's Kruger National Park is one of the continent's largest game reserves, and the abundance of wildlife is perfect for big cats.
Savannah life isn't easy, even for the mighty 'Big Five' - the lion, African elephant, leopard, buffalo, and rhino. See how their adaptations help them in daily life.
There are more species of beetle worldwide than any other animal, and few play a role as important in the ecosystem as the humble dung beetle.

Persevere with a mother crocodile as she struggles to survive and raise her young in one of Africa’s most seasonally volatile and unforgiving rivers, the Katuma. Endure hunger and danger as she guards her clutch with ruthless precision.

With seven of Ontario’s eight turtle species listed as endangered, the push is on to keep population numbers up. But turtles are slow, which means they keep taking a beating from both predators and cars. Can they be saved?
Follow the winding path across the stunning Drakensberg mountains, one of Africa's great landscapes and home to countless animals.
Voyage high into the mountain sky and discover the Cloud Mountains of South Africa, a hidden world that serves as a window to an ancient time.

Kevin Pietersen (KP) invites Matt Wright to South Africa, to visit the Kruger National Park area, and show him the state of play and understand the world of poaching. Aside from his success in cricket, KP has also been a fierce and passionate member of the global choir singing to save the rhino. It's Matt's first time in South Africa, but it's not the first time he's had to face the problem of endangered species. They will meet baby Arthur, who lost his mum to poaching alongside many other baby rhinos who suffered the same fate. Angered and emotional at this dire situation, KP and Matt seek answers to why people would do this. It's an emotional experience, and it cements the need to find solutions fast, and there may be one already. \nWhat becomes blatantly obvious is that the problem is challenging and solutions convoluted.

Kevin Pietersen (KP) invites Matt Wright to South Africa, to visit the Kruger National Park area, and show him the state of play and understand the world of poaching. Aside from his success in cricket, KP has also been a fierce and passionate member of the global choir singing to save the rhino. It's Matt's first time in South Africa, but it's not the first time he's had to face the problem of endangered species. They will meet baby Arthur, who lost his mum to poaching alongside many other baby rhinos who suffered the same fate. Angered and emotional at this dire situation, KP and Matt seek answers to why people would do this. It's an emotional experience, and it cements the need to find solutions fast, and there may be one already. \nWhat becomes blatantly obvious is that the problem is challenging and solutions convoluted.

Although the situation is bleak, there is hope.\nBack at an undisclosed reserve, Matt, KP and Graeme Smith meet another kind of team saving rhinos. From perimeter and ground-based technologies to revolutionary communication and data analysing systems, they are diving into what could be the future of wildlife conservation. Technology seems an obvious solution, but it can't be the sole strategy, so the team visit a local community who have started a wildlife tourism reserve, which blends employment with the survival of species.  It really is a war that is intensifying, and the guys witness the high level of security to protect rhinos against impending incursions at a private game reserve where another baby rhino is roaming freely with his mum. Unfortunately, it's the exception rather than the rule. Most rhinos struggle to survive. If they survive at all. The clock is ticking, and if these solutions don't work, they might all be gone by 2025.

After O'Neill and the team help relocate displaced aliens to a new homeworld, another civilisation tries to colonise the same planet, leaving the team striving to discover a fair solution to the dilemma. Sci-fi drama, starring Richard Dean Anderson and Amanda Tapping.

The members of SG-1 find themselves working in an alien power station with new identities and no memory of their former selves; as the only person who recalls their true identities, it is up to Teal'c to attempt to set things right.

Hammond orders O'Neill and the team to investigate a conspiracy theorist in Montana who claims he is an alien and in possession of a spaceship. While SG-1 is initially sceptical it begins to appear that there is some truth to his story. Sci-fi drama, starring Richard Dean Anderson and Amanda Tapping.

When a recall device is activated on a Goa'uld Death Glider that Teal'c and O'Neill are testing, the two men find themselves trapped on a several-hundred-year journey back to Chulak with only several days worth of oxygen.

When Daniel Jackson returns to Chicago to attend the funeral of his mentor, a celebrated archaeologist, he soon realizes that the death is mysteriously connected to the recent discovery of a 10,000-year-old Egyptian artifact that might be cursed.

The team undertakes a mission to disrupt an alliance between the influential System Lords Apophis and Heru'ur, while Teal'c travels to Chulak to recruit support from the Jaffa warriors in the fight against the Goa'uld. Sci-fi drama, starring Richard Dean Anderson and Christopher Judge.

General Hammond makes the shock announcement he is stepping down from his post, prompting O'Neill to investigate whether he has a hidden motive. Meanwhile, Hammond's replacement assigns Carter the task of building a planet-destroying bomb.
Ten years into the future, the former members of SG-1 must send a message into the past to prevent the extinction of the human race.
Jackson's teammates notice a disturbing change in him when he is reunited with the Harcesis child and given the Goa'uld genetic memory.

SG-1 travels to a planet to investigate a machine that induces narcotic pleasure. But when they try to leave the planet, they are overcome with debilitating withdrawal symptoms, forcing them to stay. Can they free themselves from this addiction?

During a visit to the Air Force Academy, Maj. Samantha Carter makes the acquaintance of Jennifer Hailey, a promising young cadet with a rebellious streak. Carter sees great potential in her, but Jennifer seems determined to sabotage her future with the Air Force. She is fiercely independent, opinionated and resentful of Carter, to whom she is constantly being compared.

When SG-1 sends a probe through the Stargate, a powerful electronic impulse comes back through and hides inside SGC's computer. But when the entity suddenly jumps inside Carter's mind, SG-1 must choose between saving SGC and saving Carter's life!

SG-1 encounters a tricky situation when they join forces with androids designed to look like them in a battle against an evil Goa'uld System Lord. Can they fight alongside robotic doppelgangers, or will confusion and contradiction blur the line?

SG-1 pays a visit to the Tok'ra homeworld. They arrive at Vorash on Cronos' mothership -- one of the spoils they claimed following the their recent battle with him.At a meeting with Vorash's High Council, it is revealed that SG-1 intends to lend the Tok'ra the enormous ship in order to help facilitate the Tok'ra's move to a new planet. Tanith is beside himself.
SG-1 finds themselves stranded in a crippled ship in a distant galaxy -- with Apophis threatening to destroy them.

It’s the first day of a new bluefin season, and the Gloucester captains are feeling confident, ready to put meat on deck and bring home the first fish of the season. But this year, a new fleet of grudge-holding outsiders is coming to take that all away. These incoming “tourists” are prepared to go head-to-head with the veterans and do whatever it takes to come out on top.
The Gloucester fleet defends their home turf when new boats work together to take over the competition.
Three new boats dominate the season, so the Gloucester captains put their differences aside and work together to overcome their common adversaries.
Tensions run high with a new limited quota; the competition gets personal for two rivals.
Two captains are united in grief when one of them has a death in the family, while on another boat, three generations of the same family work together to catch bluefin.
The Gloucester captains are used to dominating their home turf, doing whatever it takes to protect their waters from the imposing newcomers.

Just when the captains begin to hit their strides, bad news reaches the fleet: The bluefin markets are oversaturated, threatening to shut down the fishery. With large paychecks becoming fewer and farther between, the captains are on edge as they try to maintain momentum in a dire market. Every catch matters, because their next fish could be their last.

Due to an oversaturated bluefin tuna market, dropping fish prices are on the way to bottoming out and making the tuna worthless. The plan is to move the backlog through the market and balance supply with demand. Buyers will shut down bluefin fishing in 48 hours, forcing veterans and newcomers to push themselves to extreme measures for one more paycheck.

The bluefin market in Gloucester remains closed, but not forever. After four long days off the water, the boats get the green light to start up again, and everyone is eager to make up for lost time. But when payouts at the fishery are lower than expected, disappointment sets in across the board as the captains realize there is still a long road ahead until the market stabilizes.

With the bluefin markets reopened, it’s all hands on deck to get back in the game. As the mates in the fleet step up to prove their worth, some captains give their second-in-command free reign; others hesitate to trust their crews. As the market begins to restabilize, can captains and crews set their differences aside long enough to put meat on deck?

The captains face intense weather conditions just days after the market shut down and must decide whether it’s worth risking it all to ride out the storm or stay in and lose out on a potential paycheck. With extreme conditions and high seas beating down on the boats, and taking a toll on the captains both mentally and physically, everyone faces the ultimate choice: fight or flight?
